STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks like a medium-large dinner plate, so I estimate about 24 cm per side.
b) Reference: the chicken pieces are roughly 5-6 cm long. The plate spans about 4 chicken-lengths across the long edge, so width is about 22-25 cm.
Final width: 24 cm (area 576 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Greens (cooked chard/leafy greens with red stems and some carrot strips): they cover about 30% of the plate, roughly 175 cm². Mound thickness is about 2 cm on average (peak about 4 cm). Volume = 175 x 2 = 350 ml. Cooked leafy greens at 0.6 g/ml gives about 210 g. Thin wilted greens look lighter, so I take about 170 g.
- Chicken/fish pieces (two pieces, one golden-browned, one with a crust): together about 50 cm² footprint, average thickness 1.5 cm. Volume ~75 ml x 1.0 = about 75 g.
- Crumbs/sauce residue: a smear of about 0.3 cm over roughly 20 cm², giving about 6 ml, around 5 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: The greens look like a single layer on the plate, with no separate base layer visible. No extra hidden items are assumed.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (cooked):
- Cooked leafy greens with oil/seasoning: about 35 kcal/100 g (chard cooked with a little oil).
- Chicken or fish, cooked: about 180 kcal/100 g.
- Crumb/sauce residue: about 80 kcal/100 g.

Totals: greens 170 g → about 60 kcal; protein 75 g → about 135 kcal; residue 5 g → about 4 kcal. Total about 200 kcal, roughly 250 g.
